questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The students will learn the equations.

options.text: The equations are learned by the students.
The equation is learn by them.
The equations will be learnt by the students.
The equations by the students will be learned.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The equations will be learnt by the students.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The instructions given below should be followed while changing an assertive sentence in active voice to passive voice.

 
 
• Find the subject and object of the sentence and exchange their places; make changes in their cases as well if subject and object are pronouns.
 
• Thus, in the above sentence, *'equations' *and *'students' *will interchange their places as subject and object after conversion
 
• Use preposition by before the agent. (the students)
 
• Use an appropriate helping verb in passive form according to the tense of the active form. (Present indefinite - will be+ V3)
 
• Always use the third (past participle) form of the main verb in passive form (learnt)
 
• At last line up the remaining part

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Rachel ______ to Paris to complete her course.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **will return**

***__Key Points__**

 
• If we look at the sentence carefully, we see that the latter part of the sentence says *"...to complete her course."*, i.e., this is the **purpose**
 
• Since the purpose (of completing her course) is yet to be fulfilled, **simple future tense **would be used, i.e., **will return**
 
• Let's look at the other options:
 
 
• ***'returning': ***This is an example of a **gerund **here and it should be used alone. Thus this is incorrect.
 
• **'would returned': ****'Would' *is a **modal verb **that should be followed by **V1 (present) **form of the verb and not the past form. Thus this is incorrect.
 
• ***'was return': ***The **auxiliary verbs** *is/was/am/are/were, *etc. are followed by either **verb+ing **or **V3 + d/ed**. Thus this is incorrect.
 
 

**Thus the complete sentence is: ***Rachel **will return** to Paris to complete her course.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

A woodpecker hammering away at a tree experiences (1)/ forces in to 1,400 times that of (2)/Earth's gravity, or 1,400 G's. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• Clearly, the context explains the force experienced by woodpecker
 
• Here, the concept of preposition is brought under consideration
 
• Since 'in to' is used to denote the change of form from one to another
 
• 'up to' is used for indicating a maximum amount
 
• Thus, we should replace in to with up to

 

**Thus the correct sentence is: ***A woodpecker hammering away at a tree experiences forces up to 1,400 times that of Earth's gravity, or 1,400 G's.*
